lessonRef.focus: measuring and converting for a real task
lessonRef.title: Transfer, reflection, and publication: measuring and converting for a real task

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different setting than the problems below.

items.prompt: A runner covers 200 meters, then runs 4 more laps of 50 meters each. How many meters total?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A hiker walks 22 meters, then walks 5 more trips of 37 meters each. How many meters total?
A tank has 1477 liters of water. 9 containers of 91 liters each are drained from it. How many liters remain?
A tank has 719 liters of water. 5 containers of 56 liters each are drained from it. How many liters remain?
A tank has 1267 liters of water. 6 containers of 174 liters each are drained from it. How many liters remain?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: A hiker walks 639 meters, then walks 9 more trips of 148 meters each. How many meters total?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A hiker walks 721 meters, then walks 8 more trips of 273 meters each. How many meters total?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
